download_work_pdf.description: Download a work's PDF from CORE and keep it as a document a later step can read, attach or send on. This route needs an API key and costs more of your daily allowance than a search does. parameters.description: Ask CORE for the statistics that go with these results. It makes the response noticeably slower, so leave it off unless a later step reads them.
parameters.name: include_stats

search_works.description: Search CORE's collection of open-access research papers. A work is the paper itself: CORE deduplicates the copies it harvested from different repositories into one record, so this is the search to use for 'find me papers about X'. Filter by author, year, publication date, publisher, document type, repository, or whether CORE holds the full text. Paging reaches 10,000 records.

results.abstract: The Open Access movement has been successful in increasing the number of freely available research papers, but the potential of text and data mining over this corpus is still largely unrealised.
results.title: CORE: three access levels to underpin open access

search_works.name: search_works

parameters.description: Words to search for across every indexed field: title, abstract, authors, full text. Leave it empty and use the filters below to browse instead. CORE's own query syntax works here too: quotes for an exact phrase, AND / OR, and parentheses for grouping. Whatever you type is grouped before the filters are applied, so an OR here cannot spill into them.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only return records whose title contains this phrase. Matched as written, so it is the field to use when you know the paper.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Only return records by these authors. Every name given must appear, so adding a second name narrows rather than widens; use it to pin down a common surname by a co-author.
parameters.name: authors

parameters.description: Only return records with this DOI. A doi.org link works as well as the bare DOI.
parameters.name: doi

parameters.description: Only return records from this publisher. CORE normalises publisher names against Crossref's, so use the name as Crossref spells it.
parameters.name: publisher

parameters.description: Only return records of these types. Leave empty for every type. A record matching any one of the chosen types is included.
parameters.name: document_types

parameters.description: Only return works held by these data providers, by CORE ID. A work matching any one of them is included. 'Search data providers' returns the ID on every record.
parameters.name: data_provider_ids

parameters.description: Only return records published in or after this year. Can be used on its own for an open-ended range.
parameters.name: year_from

parameters.description: Only return records published in or before this year. Can be used on its own for an open-ended range.
parameters.name: year_to

parameters.description: Only return records published on or after this date. Use this rather than the year boxes when the window is narrower than a year; records with no exact publication date on file are excluded.
parameters.name: published_from

parameters.description: Only return records published on or before this date. Records with no exact publication date on file are excluded.
parameters.name: published_to

parameters.description: Only return records whose full text CORE has parsed. Turn this on when the workflow goes on to read the paper rather than just cite it. Note that CORE serves the full text itself only to connections with an API key.
parameters.name: full_text_only

parameters.description: Only return works that carry all of these. A quick way to ask for records complete enough for what the workflow does next: a DOI to cite, an abstract to summarise, a reference list to follow.
parameters.name: must_exist

parameters.description: Anything else in CORE's query language, ANDed onto the filters above: a field this form does not offer, a range, or an '_exists_:field' test. It is grouped before it joins the rest, so an OR inside it stays inside it.

description: Search and read CORE, the world's largest aggregator of open-access research: over 300 million papers harvested from repositories, preprint servers and journals. Find works and the repositories holding them, follow a DOI to a free copy, pull PDFs and parsed full text, count a field's output by year or author, and find the researchers working on a topic.
